headline: Models link gene expression to connectivity, network dynamics, and chromosome behavior
label: Computational Models Of Gene Expression
summary: Recent reports pair mechanistic and machine-learning models with transcriptomic, spatial, and imaging data to infer regulatory and genomic structure.
synthesis: The dominant thread across these reports is model-based inference from high-dimensional molecular measurements. CSDX links human brain gene expression to mouse connectome strength and nominates candidate protein dimers and CORUM complexes. SCOUBI uses a neural network to map axon-dendrite interfaces from extrasomatic RNA in mouse spatial transcriptomics. A systematic modelling study shows that feedback loops in gene network topologies drive recovery of heterogeneous expression from homogeneous cell populations. A semi-mechanistic ODE model of zebrafish maternal-to-zygotic transition is fitted to RNA-seq to derive expression clusters. Echidna is a Bayesian hierarchical model jointly inferring copy number alterations from scRNA-seq and bulk WGS. Shapley-explained machine learning of CRISPR-Sirius imaging places chromosome 1 loci at the nuclear periphery during serum starvation. The shared contribution is explicit model structure coupled to interpretable outputs, though the reports address distinct biological questions.
